title: Quant-aware evaluation metrics pipeline for FP8/INT8 calibration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable, reproducible evaluation pipeline that computes quality metrics for quantization profiles (FP8, INT8) and plugs into the calibration workflow. The pipeline will produce per-profile/ per-model metric bundles that the calibration service and the Console can consume.

Scope and deliverables:
- Implement stable perplexity computation for quantized checkpoints, accounting for tokenization and potential logit-scale shifts introduced by quantization. Include KL/JS divergence diagnostics against FP32 baseline.
- Integrate a MMLU-style evaluation harness that supports per-task micro/macro accuracy, aggregated pass@k and confidence-calibrated score reporting. Provide breakdown by domain and difficulty slice.
- Add Rouge and BLEU wrappers for generation tasks (summarization, translation), with configurable tokenization normalizers and detokenizers to match downstream tasks.
- Implement task-specific scorers: exact-match, F1 (QA), chrF, and a lightweight answer-normalization layer for comparison across quantized variants.
- Evaluation protocol: deterministic seeds, single-sequence vs batched evaluation modes, and a reproducibility checklist. Save raw outputs (logits, predictions) for spot-checks.
- Calibration integration: pipeline will emit calibration artifacts (scale factors, histogram summaries, layer-wise error stats) and a ranked list of profiles by quality/regression vs baseline. Include automatic regression detection thresholds and suggested rollbacks.
- CI & automation: add pipeline job in GitHub Actions and runtime-eval cluster job. Persist results to the Evaluation DB and surface key metrics in Console dashboards (links below).
- Documentation: PRD (Confluence), runbook for running local evals, and an example notebook showing how to compare FP32 / INT8 / FP8 profiles for a new model.

Acceptance criteria:
- Perplexity and MMLU harness produce stable, comparable numbers between runs (variance < 0.5% for perplexity on standard dev sets).
- BLEU/ROUGE wrappers validated on at least two datasets (WMT small subset, CNN/DailyMail) with matching baselines to within expected rounding differences.
- Pipeline emits a JSON metric bundle per profile (per-model, per-dataset) with keys: perplexity, mmlu_breakdown, rouge, bleu, task_scorers, regression_flag. Bundles are consumed by calibration service and Console mock panel.
- CI job runs in < 90 minutes for representative smoke suites; full suites run nightly and attach artifacts to the evaluation DB.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- Perplexity on quantized models can be biased by logit-scaling. We will compute both raw cross-entropy and temperature-adjusted perplexity to help diagnose this.
- MMLU-style exact-match thresholds will be configurable per dataset because quantized outputs can shift tokenization boundaries (e.g., longer subword pieces).
- FP8 vs INT8: FP8 may show lower per-token variance but different tail-behavior; evaluation will record confidence intervals and full-score distributions rather than only point estimates.
- Performance: we will support batched evaluation to speed up runs, but the default CI smoke will use single-sequence deterministic mode to ensure reproducibility.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Quant+Evaluation+Pipeline
- Evaluation notebook (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/quant-eval-examples
- GH draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2197
- Console mock dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/drafts/quant-eval-dashboard

Next steps:
1) Finalize metric schema with Console & Calibration owners (sprint week 1).
2) Implement perplexity + basic MMLU harness (sprint week 1–2).
3) Add generation scorers and CI jobs (sprint week 2–3).
4) Nightly full-suite runner and Console integration (sprint week 4).
